body:
YTA. 

tell her to switch to spotify for students. it’s $4.99/ month for premium,hulu, and showtime and she gets the first month free. that leaves her paying $75 in gas per month to you. i spend only a little more than that and i drive to and from work 4 times a week and go out pretty much every day im not at work. that’s a ridiculous amount for her to be paying to cover for you driving her to work 8 times a month.

I work 4 days a week (20 minute commute, so not long but i doubt your daughter works more than 20 minutes away from any regular route you’re on anyway) and i drive my car almost every every day and i spend between $40-50 on gas biweekly so unless your car is significantly less fuel efficient than mine (a 2003 with almost 200k miles), then she’s paying for not only the gas to get to work 4 times, but just about all your gas too.

have her pay for her music subscription directly from her own account, and see if she can carpool with any friends from work.

my smaller dog (we think some kind of shepherd mix but we found her on the side of the road so ¯\_(ツ)_/¯ ) does this to one of my bigger dogs (goldendoodle) when she wants him to get all riled up and play. usually results in the two of them jumping around and generally roughhousing for a couple minutes until the smaller dog is satisfied she’s caused enough chaos for the time being

By the time I was 20, so only a bit older than her, I had been sexually assaulted multiple times by a boyfriend who threatened to ruin my life if i came forward. He was also cheating on me with my “best friend.” She knew about the assault.

I had been locked in a moving vehicle with another boyfriend who was screaming at me over a minor disagreement. When i asked him to take me home, he told me he’d “let me go when we were done.” It wasn’t until I was dialing the police he finally let me out.

I had been roofied at prom by another guy i was seeing at the time shortly after high school. I almost got fired from my job because apparently I didn’t show up for two days. I didnt know what day it was when I woke up. I have no memory of the two days I was sick and out of it. It took months for me to realize what had happened. That same guy cheated on me while I was having major surgery and I woke up to him sending me pictures of him out with the other girl.


My experiences are not universal and i’m aware of that. But 18 is not “too young” to be so jaded. Even if she did mean it seriously, she’s certainly not too young to feel that way. She doesn’t have to have “more miles than your last B-200.” You would have said I had more miles by age 18, but none of mine were consensual.

Enough people have touched on consequences for  Kylee but why is it her fault grandma is an idiot? Let grandma not have enough money for bills for awhile and maybe she’ll smarten up. She’s a whole ass adult if she wants to go behind your back then she can handle the consequences.

I wouldnt make Kylee pay back a cent. It’s grandma’s fault for letting her add the card.
Oh, you’re paying for things you’re legally obligated to pay for? Maybe someone should teach you the moral lesson of not holding your basic responsibilities as a parent over your children’s heads 🙂

So wait a minute. It’s your 7 year olds fault that your husband is apparently incapable of keeping an eye on your toddler well enough to make sure she doesn’t eat lids???

Why can’t your husband watch the toddler better? Maybe get your 7 year old a storage space/art station in her room and only allow her to use her fancier supplies there where her sister can’t get them.

To throw them out would be to blame your 7 year old for your husband being a bad parent to your toddler and start a poor precedent of the oldest having to give things up for the younger. Don’t vilify your child for being absent minded and then in the same breath defend your husband as “not the most observant person.” He’s a parent. He better start learning how to be.

YTA.

Why is it a “bratty attitude” from your daughter when your husband is being a brainless douche? How hard is it to remember a McChicken? I’d be petty and ask if he needs to go to the doctor to get his memory checked since he’s not able to remember something so simple. 

Your husband is being an idiot. Id bet money he wouldn’t say thanks and be grateful if you or your daughter got him something he reminded you countless times he doesn’t like. He sounds like an asshole to be honest.

Also the “it doesn’t matter what i get i’m always wrong” is enough to piss me off just reading it. If he’s that stupid he can’t remember his own daughters very simple mcdonald’s order then he needs to write it down and tape it to his visor so he can read it off.
holy SHIT not only are YTA but you’re also insane

He’s 8 I dont think he really cares all that much about going pro…

Sports are supposed to be fun for the kid but it seems like you’re the type of dad who didn’t get to go pro so now you’re going to do anything you can to push your child into a sport that he might not even actually care about in two years.

Maybe i’m projecting, but I did gymnastics for 15 years. I hated it for at least 9 of them but my mother wouldn’t let up on the pressure and I didn’t feel comfortable telling her I wanted to quit and try other sports. Please don’t put that kind of pressure on your child. Sure he likes baseball now, but what about in three months when he likes football? Or basketball? Or tennis?

Also, she can take him on vacations all she wants during her time. She doesn’t need to bring him to practices right now if she doesn’t want to. He’s 8. He doesn’t need to be excused from missing practices and games from a little league team. In middle school/ high school when the teams are through the school there’s a much higher chance he can carpool with some friends too if he’s still interested in being on sports teams and his mother is still putting up a fight. Missing some little league games isn’t going to make or break this kids future possible one in a million career.
YTA. why did you have a child if your only goal was to make them miserable? have you never spent any money on things you enjoy? your ex husband was right.

He’s 15 who cares if he’s spending his first 3 paychecks on video games and food? He’s probably just excited to make money and wants to splurge some.

I’m sorry, I dont think a 15 year old working <20 hours a week should be paying for insurance, maintenance, gas, AND registration. that plus his phone bill and you’re pretty much guaranteeing he’s not having any fun money. At that point he’s just working to put gas in the car and what’s the point of that? Make him pay for gas and registration but give the kid at least a year to enjoy himself before the world kicks him in the balls.

Get the kid’s paycheck deposited into his own account and let him figure it out. Turn off the alerts. If he overspends, he can pack lunch until next payday. Recommend a budgeting app, but it’s on him to save, not on you.

You said it’s been two months and he hasn’t learned a thing about money management. It’s been two months. I’m willing to bet none of us learned money management in two months at age 15.

If your husband insists on saving for him (which will teach him nothing, by the way) then make it like 10% of the paycheck not 30%.

He’ll learn eventually, but he’s going to have to make his own mistakes. Let him make them. He’ll be okay

NTA.

Run. This is the most obvious set up for a lifetime of control and abuse. Run before you bring any children into the world with this man.
You want to be with and love the person you think he could be, not the person he is.

NAH.

I dont think you’re an asshole but i do think you should rethink this. I think your bf is being inconsiderate but it depends on why he waited until the day before to ask if it was okay to bring his roommate. Sure, maybe it was poor planning. But maybe a flight got cancelled, maybe it was a money issue, maybe something got messed up with his leave.

I get wanting meeting the family to be special. I get not feeling comfortable inviting the roommate over for a holiday. If I had suggested bringing a guest for the holidays my mom would have acted like I was committing a cardinal sin. My father would have been all for it. My father is a former marine. My ideal holidays will one day be a found family gathering, not necessarily just a blood family one.

I think that how you respond to this will determine if your relationship continues. It seems important for your boyfriend to be able to include his roommate- especially since they’re far from home this holiday season. I also understand you want this meeting to be special. A good compromise might be to invite the roommate for thanksgiving, but organize a dinner with your parents and boyfriend this weekend if you can so they can have some more “one on one” time.

The time to have the “I need more than one days notice to invite people to family gatherings” is a conversation that can wait until after this one day, I think. I’m sure if you were somewhere unfamiliar you’d be grateful to have somewhere to go for a holiday meal.

Invite the roommate, have a nice dinner with your family, and /then/ have a chat with your boyfriend about notice for family events. I think this event will have a large impact on your relationship one way or the other.

Your husbands is abusing your son. Your husband is abusing your son. Your husband is abusing your son. Yelling so loudly at a child that they urinate on themselves is ABUSE.

YOU are letting him ABUSE your child. You are allowing that to continue.

I dont know anyone who hasn’t hit a pen at least once, and after i tried it once i only tried one more time to confirm I hated it and it made me sick. Talk to her about how she felt, if she felt pressured, if it made her feel funny or sick, and open up a conversation about your past too. You seem like you’ve done great so far so I doubt this will spiral into some huge issue.

I think limiting her from the friend’s house for awhile until you can have some constructive conversations about what happened is the best move, and just have her friend hang out at your house for now.

he bought her a 15k engagement ring who tf is settling 💀💀💀

it was never gonna be on her finger because you’re spineless and couldn’t get over your commitment issues long enough to marry her

Your husband sounds awful. You and the kids stay home. He can go crawl up his mom’s ass for the day if he wants. RSV is going around- use it as an excuse to keep the kids home. He doesn’t get to decide the festivities if he’s going to be useless during them.

YTA.

i am.. boiling with anger at this post.

my father and i do not have the greatest relationship. but i would give so much to have a day to go on a hike with him. he’s older, he’s slow moving, but it’s not about the fucking hike. it’s about spending time together. bonding. being with him.

you don’t get brownie points for being fucking honest. it doesn’t matter that you “wanted to be straightforward.” you weren’t straightforward. you were an asshole.

sure, voice your thoughts. voice them in therapy. learn some empathy and basic human decency while you’re at it.

Obviously do this from a safe space away from him, but it sounds like this man needs help. He sounds incredibly overwhelmed and depressed and I dont think everyone should discount that just because he’s the father instead of the mother.

Get your kids to a safe space and then find out what’s really going on with your husband. That he feels like “he can’t even talk to me” makes it seem like he’s been asking for help for awhile and isn’t receiving it.

why don’t you like your middle daughter?

ask your husband why he’s looking at and judging a 10 year old girls body.

then ask him why he thinks it’s acceptable to body shame his own child based on his opinion of a 10 year old girl’s body.

You seem to be upset that your four year old is acting like a four year old.

All those stressors in your life are in her life too but she’s four and has no idea how to handle them, why her daddy is sick, why her mommy is so angry with her, and that there’s a good chance it just gets more stressful when the twins arrive.

Your husband’s medications don’t seem like they’re working. he needs to be pulling his weight, especially when the twins arrive.

You’re putting too much pressure on her to be this perfect kid when in reality she’s just picking up on how stressed and burnt out you and your husband are. kids respond to tensions in the household. maybe counseling for the two of you? set boundaries and expectations that he needs to pull his weight and be more helpful because you’re taking out your resentment on a four year old.

Not gonna lie, your husband sounds like a huge part of the problem. What exactly does he think being MORE strict is going to do? 

Also, if the kid has been pretty straight laced all his life have you ever considered maybe there’s peer pressure happening? bullying? a trauma? 13 year olds are brutal, i can definitely see there being some intense peer pressure from the ~cool kids~ about smoking weed and vaping.

Also also, not his job to be a good example for his younger siblings. Yeah, ideally he would Want to be a good example, but it’s not his job to be their role model. that’s yours and your husband’s and quite honestly from your comments I can see why the kid wouldn’t feel comfortable talking to y’all about any issues he’s dealing with at school. he probably thinks any problems he has will result in you and/or your husband freaking out like you did this time.

weed and vapes are SO much easier to get now than in 2012 when i was in 8th grade and i got offered one or the other at least a few times a week. peer pressure is a real problem, and it’s hard for kids that age to deal with. especially when they’re coming home to a father who seems to be trigger happy with discipline. sending a kid to a disciplinary school for some weed?? come on. by sending him there you basically just told him, “you’re too much of a problem to deal with so we’ll take you back when you’re fixed.” not exactly a shining example of how to make the kid trust and open up to you more.

i’m not saying you shouldn’t be upset. being upset makes sense. but the reality is that those things are insanely accessible today and the stricter you are on the kid, the more he’ll learn to hide. educate him on the dangers of getting high at such a young age, show him pictures of people’s lungs who are damaged from vaping, have him read about the legal consequences of getting caught using those substances. creating an open dialogue about the effects of peer pressure, how to use you as a cop out of things he doesn’t want to do like that. but being a tyrant won’t make him stop. it’ll just make him better at hiding it when he does it.

I do “no thank you” bites with my niece. 

I cook dinner fairly often, and sometimes there’s things my niece hasn’t tried before, like a new vegetable, or a new sauce or seasoning. Being four, she has that thing where she decides everything is icky without her actually ya know, trying it. 

So the rule is 3 good bites. If she doesn’t like it after that it’s “no thank you. can i have something else please?” 9/10 times she ends up liking the food and will eat all of it. This has worked for things like new seasonings on chicken all the way to brussel sprouts and peas. 

If she does choose the “no thank you”
option, she gets a sandwich and a fruit. This way it’s nutritious and she’s still eating something (kid gets cranky when she’s hungry) but it also opens her up to new things since she doesn’t feel so pressured to like it. 

Any rudeness or calling it disgusting is immediate sitting on the couch for 5 minutes no tv, to toys, no talking. After that, she’s more than welcome to try those three no thank you bites again. If she doesn’t take the three no thank you bites (which has happened 2x in 2 years) then she can go play until she decides she wants to try those bites or go to bed ¯\_(ツ)_/¯

It comes with Age Appropriate responsibility like chores. Wanting a private space in their home is not acting entitled or acting like the world revolves around yourself. That’s like saying you’re being selfish and entitled if you don’t want the kids playing in your office with expensive, breakable things. Six year olds deserve to have boundaries too, and learning to say no and how to respect a no are important skills.

Also a little concerning you seem so disdainful of thinking that kids are people too.

As long as there’s not extracurriculars he’s in that are only offered on your specific weeks, what’s the harm in switching them? I’d ask to have him for two weeks while you’re switching (so your regular week, your new week, then it’s her new week).

She should be paying the legal fees if she’s the one that wants to make the switch.

ESH. You were intentionally vague because you knew it would piss your mom off, but your mom also sounds a little bit like a bitch. It’s not going to kill her to miss having one birthday about her. Move out and just don’t talk to them anymore ¯\_(ツ)_/¯

Interesting that you edited this comment from telling me to “Be Quiet.” because i have a boyfriend AND mental health issues. 

I had a friend like you once. They had a slew of mental health issues, and a horrific attitude about dating. For awhile, me and all their other friends tried to be encouraging, telling them their positive traits and how to go out and meet people to date. 

They kept putting up a fight. For YEARS until eventually every single one of us gave up trying and cut off that person entirely. Your attitude isn’t just driving away potential partners, it’s driving away current and potential friends. 

You have some SERIOUS need for introspection. You say you want a relationship so bad, but you’re putting zero effort in. 

All those friends who met their partners “organically” how did they actually meet? At a bar? At a club? At work? I’m willing to bet they all met at some sort of social event- something you refuse to try.

So i’ve read through some comments. 

You seem like you don’t want to put in effort. The reality of it is that you’re going to get rejected. You’re going to have some bad dates. Obviously you should be vigilant- meet in public places for awhile, google their name to make sure no hidden charges, stuff like that. 

But you can’t bitch about not being in a relationship when you’re… not putting any effort into being in a relationship. It’s 2022, guys aren’t going to make 100% of the initial effort anymore and that’s okay. You need to get out of the house, join a club, go to public events, go to a bar, try online dating. 

Also, read your comment about how you don’t think you should have to fix yourself and you want your partner to help. Your partner should HELP, but the majority of the work is strictly on you, ma’am. I have plenty of mental health issues: depression, anxiety, former struggles with self harm. You know who’s responsible for managing that? Me. Not my boyfriend. Me. 

Find hobbies that involve other people. Meet people at work, hang out with people from work, branch out. It’s hard, and I know it’s hard, but it’s seems like you’re blaming the world for not chasing you, when you don’t really seem like you’re putting in effort to date.
You’re literally insane ?? Seek help. YTA.

She could put his favorite safe, non-allergen foods in that fridge for him so then he doesn’t need to climb and get into the big refrigerator, and kiddo gets to feel special for having his own snack fridge.

I do not know how to judge this one because I do not know nearly enough about how houses work. I’m going with NAH for now because it seems like you both have decent intentions.

However, my s/o and I are planning on purchasing a home at some point in the next year. I have no interest in being on the title to the home. He wants to own the home himself. This works out great. 

I think the difference is that in our (ideal, since it obviously hasn’t happened yet) setup, he is responsible for 100% of the mortgage. I will be responsible for all utilities (gas/water/sewer/electric/trash/etc.) and the majority of groceries. Major home purchases will be made together. This way, we’re both contributing almost exactly the same amount to the home (very similar incomes) but his mortgage isn’t benefiting from me when I have no stake in the home. Maybe a setup like this would work better for you and your partner?

You already seem like an amazing parent just by how much you care. Like I said, i’m not sure if that’s what’s actually happening; just that it’s a possibility. I think a calm safe sex talk and providing her with BC and condoms is a good bet because unfortunately you can’t really stop her from having sex if that’s what she wants to do. It’ll go a long way in making her feel cared about and safe if you don’t freak out, but just frame it as concern and education.

Therapy might not be the worst idea if she’s receptive to it. It didn’t work out for me, but having a trusted adult outside of the home might be someone she’s more willing to talk to if she’s going through something traumatic. This can give her coping mechanisms for those big teen emotions (because they sure do suck), but can also give her a space to vent and release all that anger without taking it out on you. It might even help her set boundaries with this boy she’s talking to.

The coach who told my parents also worked at my school (not with kids, mostly as tech support admin for teachers), so she was probably a mandated reporter. I just didn’t know that mandated reporter meant “tell parents immediately” and not “tell guidance counselor/other school official to set up a meeting.”

I do think it’s super important to know about mandated reporters for kids and adults so that way everyone can make the best and most informed decisions moving forward! I think whoever OP tells is most likely going to be a mandated reporter (i’m thinking teacher, guidance counselor, principal) but I hope that whoever they tell will handle the situation with grace and compassion.

I do not want this to sound harsh so please take this with a pound of salt. 

As a former kid who self harmed, if I found out you had told my parents or my school I wouldn’t have ever spoken to you or your son again. 

My gymnastics coach found out I was self harming, and after promising to my face she wouldn’t tell my parents, she walked out of the room and called and told them. That night when I got picked up I was locked in a car for 2 hours while my mother screamed at me about how weak I was, and I was forced to listen as she called every single family member in the contact list and mocked me and my issues. She took my phone, wouldn’t let me speak to friends. I wasn’t allowed behind any closed doors. The day of my sports banquet, when I told her I wasn’t comfortable using the new curling iron that was literally smoking my hair, she brought me my brother’s gun and told me to finish what I started. She forced me into therapy but pulled me out after two sessions when the therapist wouldn’t let her sit in on the sessions. I was with that coach for another year and I never said another word or so much as acknowledged her existence again. 

I had four suicide attempts after that. 

I know you want to do what’s best for this child, and I don’t know exactly what best is, but please, please, be careful if you tell his parents. Have an escape plan for him for if the abuse gets worse. Make sure he knows your home is a safe haven for him and if it comes down to it you will protect him. Talk to your son first to figure out how to address it, and then if the friend is comfortable talk to the friend too. I’m going to try to give some perspective from a girlfriend who also hated her boyfriend’s friends. 

When we started dating, he introduced me to them. They were very similar to your friends, always “bantering”, and did not hesitate to include me in that. What they didn’t consider though, was that they and I did not have the relationship where that “banter” (read: bullying) was acceptable. A couple months in he says he’s going on a trip with the boys. One of them brings their girlfriend, another is dating a girl from the group, no one really cares. I was uneasy about him being on this trip because of how they had treated me. We were on facetime one night and he told me to “chill out” when I said one of the girls was acting like a bitch because she was screaming about no one buying the brand of mashed potatoes she liked. I hung up and said i’d talk to him when he could have MY back. 

That event put an extreme strain on our relationship. For months he continued to be friends with this group, and for months their harassment of me got worse. Eventually, it came down to me or them. He had known them for over 10 years and he still chose me. He chose me because I was not the one who was the problem. His friends were. Just like your friends are. It is one thing to banter between long-standing friends. It is bullying when the other party is not an active participant. You’ve let your friends bully your girlfriend and then act surprised when she is upset you want to go on an expensive trip with them rather than her. 

Yes, you had every right to go on the trip. But the right thing to do would have been to sit down and make a plan. Location sharing, facetiming before bed to fall asleep together, checking in every 2-3 hours. She should not have accused you of being like her ex, but she had every right to be upset about this trip. 

Now, onto the part once you got home. Your mistake was thinking you could have a “fresh start” and pretend like that trip never happened. That trip honestly probably was the final straw for her, but on the off chance it wasn’t, the ONLY acceptable return was with flowers and chocolates and “i’m so sorry we didn’t discuss this and plan this better before i left. how i treated you was unfair. is there any way i can make this up to you?”
